source: DRAFTT is the measuring stick: each letter is a share of take-home pay against a healthy band. The `slaf` figures are Eli's own defaults, stated opinions to be overwritten in this file; the other three sources are readings of a published rule of thumb, and each note says which and how faithfully. No number here is a measured finding.
confidenceNote: Rules of thumb, not findings. A share outside a band is a prompt to look, never a verdict on a life. Where a source states no figure for a letter, the entry says so and shows Eli's default in its place.
note: Read by engines/draftt.js. Basis is take-home unless the source says `basis: gross`; the engine converts on the fly so the row always compares like with like and prints which basis is in use. `default` is the source shown until the person picks another; the pick is stored per user under prefs, never in the household. D-173.

slaf.note: Eli's default: minimums on anything but the mortgage under a tenth of take-home. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Scott Trench, Set for Life: consumer debt is the first thing to clear, so any lasting share is a fire. 5% is a reading of that stance, not a figure the book states.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show's guideline that total debt payments stay under 35% of gross income, mortgage included. Applied to non-mortgage minimums it is generous by design.

fiftythirty.note: 50/30/20 has no debt line: minimums sit inside the 50, extra payments inside the 20. 20% of take-home is the ceiling that leaves the rest of the 50 intact — a reading, not a rule from the book.

slaf.note: Eli's default: at least 15% of gross into retirement. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Set for Life's premise: save half of what you take home early on. A reading of the book's central idea.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show: 25% of gross toward retirement.

fiftythirty.note: 50/30/20: the 20 is savings and debt paydown together, of take-home. Retirement alone is a reading of it.

slaf.note: Eli's default: under a quarter of take-home. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Scott Trench, Set for Life: housing is the biggest line and the one to attack; a quarter of take-home is a reading of where he draws it.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show: housing at or under 25% of gross.

fiftythirty.note: 50/30/20: housing inside the 50 for needs; 30% of take-home is a reading of how much of the 50 it can take before food and transport are squeezed.

food.label: Food
food.sub: groceries and eating out, a month

slaf.note: Eli's default: food under 12% of take-home. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Set for Life states no food figure. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show states no food figure. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

fiftythirty.note: 50/30/20: food inside the 50 for needs; 15% of take-home is a reading of a fair share of it.

slaf.note: Eli's default: getting around under a tenth of take-home. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Set for Life: the car is the second line to attack after housing; a tenth of take-home is a reading of that, not a figure the book states.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show's 20/3/8 rule: car payments under 8% of gross. Applied here to all of getting around, so it is strict by design.

fiftythirty.note: 50/30/20: transport inside the 50 for needs; a tenth of take-home is a reading of a fair share of it.

slaf.note: Not a target — tax is what it is. Eli's default draws the line at 30% of gross so the row has a colour like the others; above it, the Tax room's levers are worth a look. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Set for Life states no tax share. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show states no tax share. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

fiftythirty.note: 50/30/20 is a split of take-home and says nothing about tax. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

slaf.note: Eli's default: under 5% of take-home, and worth every dollar under it. A stated opinion.

trench.note: Set for Life states no figure for this. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

moneyguy.note: The Money Guy Show states no figure for this. Eli's default is shown in its place, and this note says so.

citations.note: Lane 2, section 3 (L-3): where each source's figure comes from. `where` says the chapter or rule; a `reading` is the app's interpretation, not a number the source prints.

trench.value: Scott Trench, Set for Life (BiggerPockets, 2017; 2nd ed. 2023)

where.debt: Part I, chapter 2: clear consumer debt before anything else; no lasting share is stated, 5% is a reading.
where.retirement: Part I, chapters 2 to 3: save half of take-home in the first stage.
where.accommodation: Part I, chapter 3: the house hack; housing at a quarter of take-home or less is a reading of the 50% savings target.
where.food: Part I, chapter 2: food as the second controllable line; 12% is a reading, not a stated figure.
where.transportation: Part I, chapter 2: the paid-off economical car; 10% is a reading.
where.taxes: Not addressed as a share; 30% of gross is the app's default and says so.

moneyguy.value: Brian Preston and Bo Hanson, The Money Guy Show; Millionaire Mission (2024); the Financial Order of Operations

where.debt: Financial Order of Operations step 3 and the 20/3/8 car rule; a 35% of gross ceiling on all debt is the Money Guy housing-plus-debt reading.
where.retirement: Millionaire Mission chapter 1 and the show's standing rule: 25% of gross to retirement.
where.accommodation: The show's housing rule: no more than 25% of gross on housing (payment, taxes, insurance).
where.food: Not a Money Guy rule; the app carries the trench reading.
where.transportation: The 20/3/8 rule: 20% down, three-year loan, payment at most 8% of gross.

fiftythirty.value: Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi, All Your Worth (Free Press, 2005), the 50/30/20 balanced money formula

where.debt: Chapter 2: must-haves at most 50% of take-home, of which debt minimums are a part; 20% is the whole savings-and-debt-paydown share.
where.accommodation: Chapter 2: housing inside the 50% must-haves; 30% is the common reading of the housing share.
where.food: Chapter 2: groceries inside the 50%; 15% is a reading.
where.transportation: Chapter 2: inside the 50%; 10% is a reading.
where.taxes: Taxes are taken before the formula (it runs on take-home); 30% of gross is the app's default.
